bull.b: Rapid TTR franchise expansion and AMVUTTRA revenue exceeding $1B in one quarter demonstrate strong product-market fit, prescriber adoption and commercial execution. Continued first-line starts and high adherence support durable recurring revenue growth.

The shift to meaningful profitability and strong cash conversion strengthens Alnylam’s ability to fund clinical development, commercialization and partnerships internally. This reduces reliance on external capital while supporting investment in its expanding RNAi platform.

A broad pipeline across rare, cardiometabolic and other diseases creates opportunities to extend the RNAi platform beyond current products. Geographic partnerships and continued clinical milestones can diversify future revenue and improve commercialization reach.

bear.t: TTR Guidance Reduction and Demand Normalization
bear.b: The guidance cut indicates that exceptionally strong launch-period switching may not persist at the same rate. A slower underlying demand trajectory could make future growth more dependent on new indications, geographic expansion and sustained patient acquisition.

Higher royalties and substantial investment in Phase III programs and launches may limit operating leverage even as revenue grows. If pricing declines or development spending remains elevated, durable margin expansion and earnings conversion could be constrained.

The balance sheet is more stable than in 2022–2024, but meaningful debt and a recent history of losses and negative cash flow leave execution risk. A normalization of earnings could weaken coverage and reduce financial flexibility for pipeline investment.
